plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that produces goblet-shaped, crocus-like flowers in autumn, long after its strap-like leaves have died back in summer. Flowers emerge directly from the ground without foliage, giving it the nickname 'naked ladies'.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to mid autumn (September to October)
plants.location: Europe, in damp meadows and open woodlands; widely cultivated in temperate gardens in North America and Asia
plants.funFact: All parts of the plant contain colchicine, a toxic alkaloid that is also used in medicine to treat gout and in plant breeding to induce chromosome doubling.

plants.name: Aster novae-angliae
plants.description: A tall, robust native perennial with hairy stems and masses of daisy-like flowers with yellow centers. It is a vital late-season nectar source for pollinators, including migrating monarch butterflies.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to mid autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Eastern and central North America, in prairies, meadows, and roadsides
plants.funFact: New England Asters are a key fuel stop for migrating monarch butterflies, and the flower heads close up at night and on cloudy days.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A spectacular deciduous to semi-evergreen tree with fern-like leaves and large panicles of trumpet-shaped flowers that carpet streets and gardens with fallen blooms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere (October to November)
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in South Africa (Pretoria), Australia (Sydney, Brisbane), and Argentina
plants.funFact: Pretoria is nicknamed the 'Jacaranda City' because of its roughly 70,000 jacaranda trees, which turn the city purple every October.

plants.name: Sternbergia lutea
plants.description: A bulbous perennial bearing bright, crocus-like golden flowers in autumn, accompanied by dark green strap-shaped leaves. It thrives in hot, dry summers followed by autumn moisture.
plants.location: Mediterranean region, from Spain to Iran, in rocky hillsides and olive groves; cultivated in dry gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Many scholars believe this is the 'lily of the field' referenced in the Bible, owing to its bright golden flowers appearing after the first autumn rains.
